Messages.Body:
In response to the recent thread wondering why the Nos are receiving
so much hate, here is my response, wondering why the Nosferatu are
receiving so much love!

#1. Out of EVERY clan and EVERY combination of groupings, the
Nosferatu have the largest number of unique vampires available for a
grouping. (30 unique vampires available in Group 3/4). Most of the
other Camarilla clans have 27 or 28 vampires in Group 3/4 (Ventrue
have 29, including their Storyline reward Advanced Reverend Adams).
The Nosferatu got an extra Group 4 vampire in Kindred Most Wanted
(Echo) and although they only have 15 new vampires in KoT, they do
receive more Group 4 vampires than any other clan in that set.

Similarly, the Nosferatu Antitribu got an extra Group 4 vampire in
Sword of Caine (in fact, the only Group 4 vampire in that set), giving
them a slightly larger Group 2/3 than most of the other Sabbat clans.
Aside from the Assamites and !Gangrel, the !Nosferatu also have the
most number of Black Hand vampires for a given grouping (4 compared to
the typical 3 for most Sabbat clans).

Why do the Nosferatu get such special treatment in terms of the number
of crypt cards in groupings?

#2. Why do the Nosferatu get such an amazing selection of small, mid-
cap Princes?

5 - Caleros
7 - Murat
7 - Nikolaus
7 - Benjamin Rose
8 - Selma
9 - Casino
9 - Baron Dieudonne

Look at the average capacity of Toreador and Tremere Princes, most of
whom lack synergy with each other. Nos even have a better average
Prince capacity than Ventrue and Malkavian. Why is it so easy for the
Nos to field decks full of mid-cap Princes (which most of the other
clans can't do well except maybe Ventrue and Brujah)?

Plus, they also have Sheldon, the best Justicar in Group 1. And
Petrodon, one of the best Justicars in Group 5.

#3. Why do the Nosferatu get superior synergy when it comes to out-of-
clan disciplines? Have you seen the sheer amount of Auspex, Dominate,
and Fortitude available in their more recent groupings? Add in the !
Nos, and the results are jaw dropping:

Group 3:

Nos: AUS aus aus aus
Nos: for for for for

!Nos: AUS aus
!Nos: DOM dom
!Nos: for

Group 4:

Nos: aus aus
Nos: DOM dom dom
Nos: FOR for for

!Nos: aus aus
!Nos: DOM dom
!Nos: FOR FOR for for for for

Group 5:

Nos: AUS AUS AUS aus
Nos: DOM dom
Nos: for

I don't think any other clan even comes even close when it comes to
synergy of out-of-clan disciplines. Have you ever looked at the out-of-
clans for the Toreador? It's a complete mess! Why do the Nosferatu get
such special, favored treatment, which lets them build really strong
decks based on common out-of-clans? (And AUS or DOM takes care of the
bleed defense issue).

#4. When it comes to Keepers of Tradition:

- Why do the Nos get an extra Group 4 vampire?

- Ruxandra is so broken in stealth bleed decks, since she lets you
discard all of your excess stealth each turn.

- Gustaphe is sooo overpowered. He's like Beast, but so much better!
ANI is more useful than OBF when it comes to combat. Gustaphe's DOM
gives him bleed potential and bleed defense. Gustaphe can use action
cards, have equipment, and have retainers. And he's titled which gives
him access to cards and makes him immune to several effects. (Beast
costs one less pool, can rush cross-table, and has +1 strength). But
Gustaphe easily outclasses Beast overall, IMO.

- Why is Zelios so much better than Bloody Mary and Allanzan Serata?
(Hint: Free, useful special)

- Yes, Josef sucks, but Petrodon is one of the best new Group 5
Justicars. Easily better than Gabrielle and Montecalme. I think only
Mary Anne can compare.

- Nosferatu also get the best clan card in this set (Warsaw Station).
Works especially well with the Labyrinth.

--> So it seems so clear that the Nosferatu *must* be one of LSJ's
favorite clans, cause they're definitely getting sooooo much love! Why
are so many of the other clans being left out? I tell you, it isn't
fair!!! (Yes, there's a hint of sarcasm in this post, if you can't
tell!).

Well, I should wait til I see it, I guess. But in a card game, I
think it is best to let the cards tell the story.

In any event, I think caution should be exercized in adapting "canon"
RPG material. Remember that V:tM supplements were merely intended as
aids to the Game Master, who remains in charge and is the final
arbiter of what goes in and stays out. Ultimately, it remains the
Game Master's job to create a credible world, and resolve the various
threads. It was also the Game Master's job (together with the
players) to create characters. Richard Garfield's idea to just create
his own characters was perfectly in keeping with the spirit of V:tM.

If no discretion is exercized, then what one ultimately ends up with
is too many cooks spoiling the broth, resulting in a formless mess.
No sooner does one V:tM writer try to lay down a rule, than another
V:tM writer comes along and decides it would be really creative to
break that rule.

think the Nossies with maybe like a handful of exceptions, look

an overwhelming minority compared to whole that could even be debated
as "normal." But that just goes back to definition.

I think the statement, which I do not feel is quite accurately quoted,
should be read and understood in its context, where I explain what I
meant by it. Certainly, being a Nosferatu fan SHOULD give one's
opinions more weight, when it comes to Nosferatu, just as a V:tES
fan's preferences should have greater weight when it comes to V:tES.
An M:tG fan's preference may be "equally valid", but if he is going to
play M:tG anyway, why change V:tES to suit him? Similarly, why change
the Nosferatu to suit those who prefer Toreador?

But if you are trying to convict me of actually preferring my own
opinions, on some level, you are liable to succeed. "Every day one
comes across somebody who says that of course his view may not be the
right one. Of course his view must be the right one, or it is not his
view." (GK Chesterton, on "The Suicide of Thought"). To suggest that
a man may not believe his own opinion is any way preferable to someone
else's opposing is really the ultimate in intolerance, because the
suggestion essentially seeks to ban all opinions..

But in this context, I have said nothing to suggest that those who
prefer vampires that are more normal looking, more subtly vampiric,
more subtly monstrous, should not get exactly what they want. If they
prefer Toreador, or Brujah, or Malkavians, or Ventrue, of Gangrel,
they should get those clans. I said nothing to imply their opinion is
less valid.

What I objected to was having those who prefer other clans effectively
ban the Nosferatu from the game by turning the Nosferatu into the sort
of vampires they prefer. Their opinions may be "equally valid" in
some sense, but there are over 2 dozen other clans in the game through
which they may explore their "equally valid" preferences. The
Nosferatu may be a minority preference, but they were never meant to
be anything else -- they constitute only one out of the original seven
clans.

Other vampires are already prone to pallor; they already have scary
fangs when they choose to bare them; they are already prone to the
drives of the Beast, that tend to turn them into monsters.

Look at Yorik, from the first Sabbat set. His features seem normal
enough, but he seems to be in the grip of the Beast, and his mouth is
wide open in a fanged snarl. He is a Malkavian Antitribu, which works
fine for this sort of vampire. The Nosferatu are not needed to fill
this Niche, or to indulge this "equally valid" preference.

Look at Roland Bishop, from the original set. His pale wrinkled face
ain't pretty, but if he draws in his fangs and wipes the blood off his
chin, he should have no trouble walking into a convenience store to
buy some smokes. He is Malkavian (though I suspect the artist may
have intended Gangrel).

I could give other examples from earlier sets that might arguably be
used as Nosferatu if used today (Rake, Yuri the Talon, Ricki van
Dempsi, Brazil, Dan Murdock, Melek, Franciscus, Petru Sipos, Salbatore
Bokkengro, Cameron, Horatio, Frederick the Weak, Hugo, Jacko, Jacob
Bragg, Luther, Rex). Judging by some cards, current standards deem so
forgiving that I could probably list many more.

By using these sort of portraits to represent the Nosferatu, we are
not gaining anything we did not have before. We are simply losing the
original conception of the Nosferatu.

Those are your words, not mine. I'd rather just say I don't like the
idea. The key word here, I think, is "portrait". The idea is to
depict the vampire -- or at least it used to be. And if I am going to
rate the portraits as portraits (which is what I have been doing) then
I am going to take off points from those that are unsuccessful in
depicting their subject.

I like the idea that the portraits represent the vampires, and other
cards represent the powers that they use. This is achieved, for
instance, when Smudge bleeds, and then Lucretia masks the bleed --
everyone gets the thematic idea that Lucretia was using her obfuscate
powers to look like Smudge. This does not mean it would be a clever
idea to use Smudge's portrait for a Nosferatu crypt card. At least I
don't think so.

One could design a card called "Jakob the Elusive" and for its
"portrait" depict an empty night-time street. I might get the joke --
I might even find it preferable to a picture of a normal dude (since
it allows me to imagine the Nosferatu it fails to depict). But as a
picture of a Nosferatu, it should get pretty low marks, to say the
least.

There is also value in consistency. It was established early on, with
the Group 1 Nossies, that the portrait represents the unmasked vampire
-- as he actually is -- as ancient powerful Methuselahs (the Players)
could perceive him. Breaking this rule only creates thematic
confusion.

It's really just a standard RPG setup. The PLAYERS are not supposed
to know much. The STORYTELLER is the one who knows the Truth, and he
gets to decide what the Truth is. The "Truth is Out There" but it is
for the Storyteller to know and the Players to find out. It does not
necessarily mean the game designers are espousing nihilism -- such
would in fact be very boring, for it would mean, in the final
analysis, that there were no mysteries for Players to solve.

But, in any event, V:tES is NOT meant to be a game experienced from
the perspective of a typical V:tM player. The player's perspective --
that of a powerful, ancient , 4th Generation Vampire -- is far closer
to the perspective of the Storyteller. We are the guys who know
what's going on.

much of a good thing is bad, but rather that too much of a bad thing

compensate. The better the artist's work (whether the art be a
picture or the game as a whole), the more the player or fan will be
inspired to participate.

Nosferatu portraits are illusions generated by obfuscate, and then
obtain pictures that represent what I imagine to be their true
appearance, and paste these pictures over the original oval
portraits. But if I do that, it is certainly no complement to the
original artwork.

deformed monstrosities. To present a normal person as a Nosferatu, on

mollify those who are embarrassed by the Nosferatu, and wish they did
not exist (such as the "monsters are for kiddies" crowd, who

immortals). But it will hardly do much for those who appreciate the
clan to begin with.
